title: AWS Cloud Practitioner
subtitle: Understand, use and estimate the core services of Amazon Web Services
audience_line: IT staff, developers, students and managers starting with AWS
overview: This programme gives participants a working knowledge of Amazon Web Services and prepares the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner exam (CLF-C02). They learn the cloud models and AWS pricing, secure an account with IAM, then use the core services: networking with VPC, Route 53 and CloudFront, compute with EC2, Lambda and containers, storage, databases, scaling and monitoring, all framed by the Well-Architected Framework. Every chapter ends with a lab in the AWS console or CLI, exam practice closes the content, and the programme ends with a final project in which teams deploy a highly available web application and present its cost estimate.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: IT staff, developers, students and managers starting with AWS

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: None. Basic IT literacy; networking or Linux basics help but are not required

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 33 h: 27 h of chapters + 6 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs in the AWS console and CLI; exam practice

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per participant with a browser and the AWS CLI; one AWS sandbox account per team, provided by the organiser, with a budget alert; resources destroyed at the end of each lab to control cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase, practice exam questions and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete the labs and the project

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can explain and choose the core AWS services, deploy a simple highly available web application, estimate its cost and sit the CLF-C02 exam

phases.name: Cloud Concepts & Security
phases.focus: Cloud models, pricing and global infrastructure, IAM
phases.intro: Participants learn what the cloud changes, how AWS charges for it and where it runs, then secure their sandbox account: the shared responsibility model, IAM users, groups, roles and policies, and MFA. Validated lab: an account with MFA on the root user, an administrators group, a least-privilege role and a cost budget with an alert.

chapters.title: Cloud Concepts
chapters.content: Service and deployment models, benefits of the cloud

chapters.title: Economics & Global Infrastructure
chapters.content: Pricing models, total cost of ownership, billing, Regions, Availability Zones, edge locations

chapters.title: Security & IAM
chapters.content: Shared responsibility, users, groups, roles, policies, MFA

phases.name: Core Services
phases.focus: VPC, Route 53, CloudFront, EC2, Lambda, containers, storage, databases
phases.intro: Participants build with the services most workloads use: a VPC with public and private subnets, DNS and content delivery, virtual machines, functions and containers, object, block and file storage, and relational and NoSQL databases. Validated lab: a web server in a public subnet serving images from S3, with its database in a private subnet.

chapters.title: Networking & Content Delivery
chapters.content: VPC, subnets, security groups, Route 53, CloudFront

chapters.title: Storage
chapters.content: S3 and its storage classes (including S3 Glacier), EBS, EFS

phases.name: Architecture, Operations & Exam Preparation
phases.focus: Well-Architected Framework, load balancing, Auto Scaling, CloudWatch, CLF-C02 practice
phases.intro: Participants judge an architecture against the six pillars of the Well-Architected Framework, make it scale and heal with Elastic Load Balancing and Auto Scaling, watch it with CloudWatch, then practise exam questions across the four CLF-C02 domains. Validated lab: an Auto Scaling group behind a load balancer that replaces a stopped instance, with a CloudWatch alarm.

chapters.title: Scaling & Monitoring
chapters.content: Elastic Load Balancing, Auto Scaling, CloudWatch

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A highly available web application and its cost estimate
phases.intro: Teams of two or three deploy a highly available web application in their sandbox account from a written brief, reusing the phase labs, then present the architecture and its monthly cost as they would to a manager.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, draw the architecture, then deploy the VPC, EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer, RDS database and S3 bucket

chapters.title: Monitor & Estimate
chapters.content: CloudWatch alarms, a budget, a cost estimate with the AWS Pricing Calculator, architecture diagram

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live demo with an instance failure, cost presentation, teardown; questions and feedback

project.title: A Highly Available Web Application on AWS
project.brief: A web application that survives the loss of a server: a VPC across two Availability Zones, an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer, an RDS database, static content on S3, CloudWatch alarms and a budget, presented with its monthly cost estimate.
project.stack: AWS: VPC, EC2, Auto Scaling, Application Load Balancer, RDS, S3, CloudWatch, AWS Budgets, AWS Pricing Calculator
project.deliverable: Working deployment, architecture diagram, cost estimate, live demo
